**Tests.** `PermissionCloseTest` (core, 10): a permission named with the warning on every seat; a
leave named without it and never closing, before and after the warning; Bluetooth switched off
and a reset never counting; three permissions in one shift one warning and no close; a leave then a
permission from one seat named once, warned; a permission after the warning closing the house for
every seat, the Insider's, the Revoked seat's and the host's, with one effect each and every later
report refused; the close at the meeting that warned; an out seat neither warning nor closing while
the host does both; a new round starting with no warning, after a warning and after a close; the
close permitted only to the ended round. `PermissionWarningTest` (ui, 5): the owner's words with one
name and two, drawn on the notices screen; a leave's notice unchanged; the warning reset between
rounds; the close walking a guest to JOIN A HOME from four screens, Insider and Resident, living and
out, with the same two lines, drawn on JOIN A HOME; the host back on its lobby, still hosting, the
two lines drawn there. `PermissionCloseRecordingTest` (harness, 2): the cause, the warning, the close
and the three columns survive the text form and replay identically; a role exchange adds no
unexplained divergence. `PermissionCloseLoopbackTest`
(app, 1, real sockets): the evening end to end, below. `ContactUploaderTest` (app, +4): a trip to
Settings that switched a grant off goes up as a permission and one that did not as a person's; a
grant off at arming never counts; a grant read off late is its own report once until it is back on;
a relaunch compares against the grants kept at arming. `PermissionsTest` (platform, +1): one bit a
row, a refusal only. `SwitchboardRadioTest` (platform, 3 changed): Unauthorized is now
`Permission`. `RangingPoolTest` (model, 2 changed): `NotAllowed` is now `Permission`. Fixtures that built a notice name the field (`RadioFaultTest`, `RoundWireTest`,
`HouseNoticeTest`, `HousedContentTest`, `HouseBuzzTest`, `EvasionNoticeTest`,
`ContactRadioBenchTest`); `RoundWireTest`'s one-of-every-effect fixture gains the close; the
admission test's origin table names the close as the radio's.

**The loopback evening** (`aSecondPermissionClosesTheHouseOnEveryPhoneAndALeaveNeverDoes`): host and
three guests, armed through production's arming path. Mia goes to Settings and switches a grant off:
her report goes up as a permission, the house's log says `PERMISSION`, and the next meeting names her
with the warning, the same bytes and the same words on every phone. Jo then only leaves the app: a
person's report, no close, named at the next meeting without the warning. Jo then switches a grant
off: the house closes, every phone is pushed the close once in the same bytes, every guest lands on
JOIN A HOME with the two lines, unattached and out of the round, and the host lands on its lobby,
still hosting, with the two lines, its standing back to one seat; no guest is sent `RoundEnded`.

**Renders** (`PermissionCloseRender`, 600×1300, `ui/build/screens/permission-*.png`). Looked at, each:
`permission-notice-warned-one` (the notices band, and in its box *Resident MIA was unreachable this

Everyone starts over.* in the refusal slot's body type, where ROUND IN PROGRESS is drawn); and
`permission-closed-host-lobby` (the host's lobby unchanged, settings and YOUR ONE LINE, and the same
two lines centred above LIGHTS OUT). No new light, colour or type on any of them.

**Not on a phone.** Nothing here has run on one. The checklist (`phone-session-2026-11-19.md`)
gains a line: mid-round, switch a permission off in Settings and come back, and the next meeting's
notice carries the warning; switch one off again on any phone, and every phone shows THE HOUSE IS
CLOSED and returns to JOIN A HOME, the host's to its lobby.

**Limits, reasoned and not observed:**

1. **A guest that did not see the close** (suspended, or its socket failed, at that moment) comes
   back to a house on the next round: the turnover wiped the retained pushes (V2), so it is not
   replayed the close, and the next standing walks it to the host's lobby (V1, D-267) without the two
   lines. Nothing is stuck; the words are missed.
2. **A guest whose close and a later standing arrive in one read** (another guest hung up first, and
   this one's socket stalled) ends its round on the standing before the close's push is applied, and
   lands on the lobby the same way. The host sends the standing only after a guest has left, so this
   needs a stall of at least one round trip.
3. **Notifications answers late.** If the first beat after a return reads the grant before iOS's
   callback lands, the leave goes up as a person's and the permission as its own report a beat
   later: the seat is still listed for the warning, by a second report.

**Decisions for the owner** (each provisional):

1. **Bluetooth switched off is not a permission** (above): named, never counted. Toggling Bluetooth
   off in Control Centre is evasion D-187 names, and the ruling's word is *permission*; the Perms
   seam already reads a powered-off radio as granted.
2. **Nearby Interaction refusing a session is a permission switched off** (above), as D-309's gate
   makes it: a phone in a round was seated with NEARBY DEVICES GRANTED.
3. **A grant switched off in the lobby, before arming, does not count**, except Bluetooth's, which the
   radio reports as a permission at the round's first advertise (D-223's *already off at arming* rule).
4. **An out seat neither warns nor closes**, the host's excepted, by D-242's and D-289's rule for who
   the notice names.
5. **The close's two lines are drawn in the refusal slot of the screen each phone lands on** (JOIN A
   HOME, or the host's lobby), the existing closed house's place for its line, rather than on a screen
   of their own before it: a screen of their own would need a timing value or a control the ruling
   does not give.
6. **A guest is not dismissed**: it hangs up and keeps its seat token, so JOIN takes it back into the
   host's next lobby by that token. *Everyone starts over* is the new round, not new seats.

### D-311 · **Anything this game needs switched off counts, the Bluetooth radio included: in the lobby the phone is let go to PERMISSIONS, mid-round it is named in the owner's new permission sentence, and after the warning it closes the house; leaving the app never counts — built (recording 46)**

**The rulings** (owner, 2026-11-21; the details approved: *"lgtm, build it"*):

- *"The game requires all these to function. Turning them off would be cheating. If you're in the
  lobby you get kicked out and land on the permission screen. If you are mid-game a reworded
  permission message shows and the same warning is stated about if it happens again the game will
  end."*
- **What counts as switching off:** any permission PERMISSIONS asks for (CAMERA, BLUETOOTH, NEARBY
  DEVICES, MOTION & FITNESS, NOTIFICATIONS) withdrawn in Settings, **and the Bluetooth radio itself
  turned off** (Control Centre, or airplane mode). Leaving the app (the side button, swiping home,
  another app) is still not switching off: named as unreachable, never counted.
- **In the lobby, before lights out:** switching any of them off removes the phone from the lobby,
  and it lands on PERMISSIONS with that row refused; with everything back on, it rejoins as usual.
  The same check runs at lights out, so no phone enters a round missing one.
- **Mid-round, the words, approved verbatim:** *"Resident Mia switched off a permission this game
  needs. If anyone switches one off again, the house closes and everyone starts over."*, and for two
  or more *"Residents Mia and Jo switched off a permission this game needs. If anyone switches one
  off again, the house closes and everyone starts over."*, the names joined as the existing notice
  joins them. **These replace D-310's appended two sentences.** Seats that only left the app keep
  the existing sentence, unchanged, **and it comes first**; a seat that both left and switched off is
  named once, in the permission sentence.
- **The second time** closes the house exactly as D-310 built it.

**D-310 overruled, item by item:** its provisional decision 1 (*Bluetooth switched off is not a
permission*) is **overruled by the ruling**: the radio turned off counts exactly as a permission
switched off. Its provisional decision 3 (*a grant switched off in the lobby, before arming, does not
count*) is **overruled**: in the lobby the phone is let go, and a grant off when a round arms is
counted (below). Its words (*"A permission was switched off. If anyone switches one off again…"*,
appended to the leavers' sentence) are **replaced** by the permission sentence. Decisions 2, 4, 5 and
6 stand.

**What counts, on the phone.** `causeOf` reads **Off as `RadioCause.Permission`**, as it already read
Unauthorized; Resetting and Unsupported stay the phone's own (D-223) and still win a disagreement. So
the round's radio reports Bluetooth turned off as a switch-off, through the one fixed body
(`permit`, D-217), and the house's rules, schema and close are D-310's, unchanged: the rules never
knew which grant it was and still do not. **How Bluetooth's power is read:** two ways, both from
CoreBluetooth's own `poweredOff` state.

1. **In a round**, the contact radio's two managers (`SwitchboardRadio`, D-218) report `Off`, and
   the onset goes up as a switch-off.
2. **Everywhere, the lobby included**, the Perms seam's own `CBCentralManager` (`Permissions.ios`).
   It was built only by the BLUETOOTH row's request, so a phone that skipped PERMISSIONS (D-235) held
   none; it is now built at the launch refresh and every re-read once the grant is `allowedAlways`
   (so no permission prompt), **with iOS's power alert switched off**
   (`CBCentralManagerOptionShowPowerAlertKey` false: the game's answer is the PERMISSIONS row, not
   iOS's modal). `Permissions.bluetoothOff()` is its `state == poweredOff`. **`Permissions.standing`**
   reads a BLUETOOTH grant given while the radio is off as **REFUSED**, and every reader takes it:
   the rows and the gate (`PermsModel(read = permissions::standing)`, the request through
   `requestStanding`), `missing()` and `refusedGrants()`. The grant itself (`grant`) is unchanged: a
   powered-off radio is still one the app may use, and the log says `THE RADIO IS OFF (D-311)`.

**Unverified until a phone shows it:** since iOS 11 Control Centre's Bluetooth button is
documented as disconnecting accessories rather than powering the radio off. If iOS keeps the radio
powered for it, neither manager hears `poweredOff`, and nothing is named, because nothing the game
needs went off. Airplane mode does power it off. The phone session checks which.

**The lobby** (`FlowModel.permissionsChecked`). Asked of the OS by a fresh read of the rows
(`PermsModel.switchedOffNow`: the rows reading REFUSED, the radio off among them; a seated phone
passed the gate with every row GRANTED, so what it lacks now was switched off). Called by the app
root once a second (`LOBBY_CHECK_MILLIS`, provisional: Control Centre suspends nothing, so no
foreground watch hears it), on every return to the foreground after `Permissions.reread` answers
(D-310's read, no probe), and on every arrival in a lobby (NEW ROUND, a later round's push, the host
after a close). It acts only on a phone holding a lobby seat, standing on the lobby or the one-line
screen, and not holding a round seat (below); anywhere else it moves nothing. **No Nearby Interaction
probe starts for it** (D-309): the read is of what the seam holds; landing on PERMISSIONS runs that
screen's own refresh, as it always has.

- **A guest** leaves the lobby as LEAVE does (it hangs up, keeps its seat token and its name), the
  rows are read in place (`PermsModel.readNow`, no probe) so the row switched off reads REFUSED on
  arrival, and it is pushed to PERMISSIONS with nothing behind it. The house's desk drops it from the
  standing, so the round armed at LIGHTS OUT does not hold it. Back on, CONTINUE and a tap on the home
  take it back in by its token, as usual.
- **The host** (provisional, the coordinator's suggestion, chosen as the least disruptive): the host
  is the house, so leaving would end every guest's lobby. It is **shown PERMISSIONS with the house
  still on the air and every guest still seated**; it cannot press LIGHTS OUT from there, and
  `lightsOut` asks the same question again at the press (a host holding LIGHTS OUT with something
  off arms nothing and is shown PERMISSIONS). Back on, its CONTINUE goes back to its own lobby
  (`PermsScreen`: `Lobby` when hosting, `Join` otherwise; declared in `Flow.viaActions`). No new copy:
  PERMISSIONS draws its rows and the gate's sentence (THIS PHONE CANNOT TAKE A SEAT YET / the rows)
  as ever.
- **NEARBY DEVICES in the lobby** is heard only if something reads it: a refusal stands in the
  seat's last probe, and the lobby starts none. Switched off in the lobby without a relaunch, it is
  heard at lights out, when the round's ranging sessions refuse, and named at the first meeting.

**At lights out.** The host's own phone is checked at the press (above). A guest's phone cannot be
asked by the host without a new lobby message, and none is added: each guest is checked on its own
phone, once a second and on every return, and one that is missing something has already left the
lobby before the press. **For the moment between a guest's last check and the arming**, the uploader
no longer excuses a grant that is off when the round arms (D-310 compared against the arming read):
one off then goes up on the first beat as a switch-off and is named at the first meeting, as the
radio already reported a Bluetooth still off at arming (D-223). So no phone plays a round missing one
unnamed. **Provisional:** a lobby message saying *not ready* would keep that guest out of the round
instead; it is a wire change and was not made.

**The notice.** `Effect.NoticeIssued` and `RoundMessage.NoticeIssued` carry **two lists, no seat on
both**: `unreachable`, the seats named that only left the app, and `switchedOff` (was
`permissionSwitchedOff: Boolean`), the seats named that switched something off. The rules partition
the named seats at the check-in gate (`checkedIn`): a seat on `GameState.switchedOff` goes on the
permission list alone, the rest on the leavers'. The warning is given when the permission list is
not empty. The state rows are unchanged (`unreachable` still lists every named seat, `switchedOff`
the subset), so the partition is the effect's alone. **The wire:** one frame, the same bytes on
every phone (D-217); the schema row is unchanged (`NOTICE_ISSUED` to `LIVING + OUTSIDE`: the field
rides the kind it is part of, and an effect with no row still ships to nobody). **The words**
(`noticeBody(names, switchedOff)`, `ui`): the leavers' sentence, unchanged, then the permission
sentence (`SWITCHED_OFF_A_PERMISSION`, `IF_ANYONE_SWITCHES_ONE_OFF_AGAIN`), the names joined with
commas then *and* by `residentsNamed`, the verbless twin of `residents`. `PanelState.noticeSwitchedOff`
is the list, reset between rounds. `PERMISSION_WARNING` is gone. No new light, colour or type: the
notice's own box and type.

**Recording: 46.** The `NoticeIssued` effect row's `unreachable=` now lists the leavers alone and its
`switchedOff=` a list of seats where it was `true`/`false`, so a version 45 recording's notice rows
cannot be compared with what this build emits (a 45 row naming a switcher under `unreachable=` would
read as a leaver). Events and state rows are unchanged; the radio turned off arrives as the cause
`Permission`, which a 45 build already parses. A version 45 recording is refused, as every older one
is.

**Found by the overnight review** (2026-11-21, relayed by the coordinator; each with a test that was
red before its fix and is green after):

1. **CONFIRMED, fixed: a relaunch turned a leave into a second permission and could close the
   house.** `ContactUploader` reset what it had reported to nothing on every seed and kept only the
   arming read, so after one reported switch-off, with the grant still off, a leave and a relaunch
   went up as `Permission`; and `RangingPool.open` forgets its refusal, so a relaunch with NEARBY
   DEVICES still off raised a fresh onset. **Fix:** what was reported this round is one bit a grant
   (`reported`), **kept beside the owed reports** (the `grants` line, which D-310 used for the arming
   read) and read back on the relaunch; the record is kept while anything is reported, not only
   while something is owed. The pool's refusal is the NEARBY DEVICES bit, so the pool's fresh onset
   after a relaunch, and the launch probe reading the row refused, are both the bit already told.
   **Test:** `ReviewRelaunchTest` (the reviewer's, copied in unchanged) — before (the reviewer's run on D-310's tree, and here with the fix reversed, `reported = 0` on the seed): *a leave after a relaunch went up as a second permission switched off. Expected <[Person]>, actual <[Permission]>*;

   by a relaunch over real sockets (a fresh process on the old files, cold-started on the self-test,

### D-313 · **Overnight fixes where the code contradicted a ruling (2026-11-21) — built**

An audit found code that contradicts rulings already made. Each fix below has a test that failed
before it and passes after. No new copy, and no light, colour, type or timing value changed. The
wire did not widen and the recording did not change.

1. **An early Drift tap is handed over and graded REJECTED** (D-165, superseding E-S2-3). The screen
   handed a tap over only after the buzz, so a tap before it was echoed and the player could try
   again: a free probe of the house's NOW. A tap before the buzz now goes as
   `ChoiceEntry.handOverEarly`, the mark stays where the finger landed, `RETURNED . WAITING` shows,
   and a second tap moves nothing and sends nothing. **What goes is an entry holding no step**
   (**provisional (overnight)**): the screen is the only thing that knows the house had not asked,
   and an entry of the wrong shape is graded wrong (`Subroutines.within`), so the house rejects it
   whatever the dot was doing. Nothing reads a role. `DriftScreen`'s KDoc no longer argues E-S2-3.
   `SubroutineMotionTest.driftEchoesATapBeforeTheBuzzAndSendsOnlyTheOneAfterIt` is rewritten as
   `driftHandsOverATapBeforeTheBuzzAndTheAttemptIsGone`, walked for both roles with the two wires
   compared. Before: *Resident: a tap before the buzz was kept back, so the player may try again
   for free (D-165)*. After: passes. The house's half, `EarlyDriftTapTest`, holds today (empty entry
   REJECTED, attempt spent, both roles alike) and stays as a guard.
2. **A Surge takes no input** (D-182: *player input: none*). The slam is a lamp drawn over the
   panel, and it holds no finger. In the bright phase a tap on Drift's lane handed the entry over,
   and in the dark phase STOP NOW sent `StopSubroutine`. Two changes. While a Surge runs, `Screen`
   puts a pane over everything that consumes every pointer (`inputBlocked`, passed by `FlowHost`).
   And `FlowModel.surged` lets go of the card at the slam rather than at the reboot, so a gesture
   already under way (a Short's hold running out) cannot hand work over either
   (**provisional (overnight)**: the ruling says the work is lost and does not say in which phase).
   `SurgeTakesNoInputTest`. Before: *a tap in the Surge's bright phase handed the Drift over …
   [HandOverEntry(marker=card-hall, entered=[])]* and *a tap in the Surge's dark phase put something
   on the wire … [StopSubroutine]*. After: passes. With the slam's let-go removed on purpose, the
   in-flight case fails: *a gesture that began before the Surge handed work over during it … entered=[2],
   … entered=[3]*. **Limits, not fixed:** a hold on page 2 already under way when the Surge lands
   (arming a Revoke or an Egress, the report circle) still completes, because a pointer already down
   keeps its target. And on the scan screen the cheats build's camera window stays open through the
   bright and dark phases, so a card read there still goes up. Closing it at the slam would move
   the double vibrate the window gives on closing from the reboot to the slam, and no ruling says
   which.
3. **Rules that held with nothing pinning them now have tests.** Each was broken on purpose once and
   restored:
   - **D-154: a Revoke leaves System Integrity where it was**, with the meter moved once before and no
     meter push riding the touch. Broken (a landed Revoke decrements the meter): *a Revoke moved System
     Integrity (D-154: the meter moves on completions only) expected:<39> but was:<38>*.
   - **The Insider's fake advances its own work order and not the meter.** Broken (only a banked
     entry marks its line done): *an Insider's accepted fake left its line of the work order standing
     expected:<true> but was:<false>*.
   - **D-143 at eighteen seats: the band is 3..5**, and a hand-picked 1 or 2 is clamped to 3. Broken
     (the floor capped at two, which no other test catches): *eighteen seats are not the D-143 band
     3..5 expected:<3..5> but was:<2..5>*.
   - **Surge is the Access pool's longest weight over Static too**, and Static stays above the 60 s
     of the ability it replaced (D-186). Broken (Static at 150 s): *Static is now at least as heavy
     as Surge, so Surge is no longer the Access pool's longest*. The ordering in force is the build's, Surge 150 > Static 120 >
     Isolate 90. Surge over Isolate and Static over Isolate were already pinned, so this was the
     missing pair. No ruling puts Isolate above Static.

**Stopped: unregistered cards in a round (D-124, D-169).** The contradiction is real. A card not
registered in this home goes up as `BeginSubroutine` and the rules answer it NOTHING FOR YOU HERE,
when D-124 reserves NOT A MARKER for it. On the way, the rules place the seat at a card that is no
place in the home and spend whatever it had armed, though D-072 says unregistered paper never
reaches the rules. A mislaid meeting card calls a meeting, because `CallMeeting` carries no card
and admission checks none. D-169 says it is refused as unregistered, and `inRoundScan`'s KDoc
claims, wrongly, that the rules refuse it. **The fix needs a decision no ruling makes.** A phone has
no map, so only the house can route a scan (`routeScan`). That takes a card id on the meeting
card's request, which is an uplink change. It also takes a way to tell one phone NOT A MARKER,
which is a new downlink member or field with an emit-schema row. And D-072's *no event* means that
answer would be a delivery outside the recording. All three are *what a client may receive* and
*whether something needs a schema entry*, which `project-context.md` says to ask. **For the
owner:** one raw-read request from the scan, routed by `routeScan` at the authority, plus a
scanner-only unregistered answer that is not recorded, or another shape. The acquire buzz is D-160's
*acquired = yes* and stands either way. Whether NOT A MARKER also buzzes *no* is unruled.

### D-314 · **Overnight: the permission walk survives a late answer, and the simulator benches play again (2026-11-21) — built**

**What the overnight run found.** Both multi-simulator scripts stopped at the lobby on every seat:
`SETUP INCOMPLETE AFTER 15S — STILL MISSING NEARBY DEVICES`, then `NOT HOSTING — THIS PHONE CANNOT
TAKE A SEAT YET / NEARBY DEVICES`. No `[perms]` line for NEARBY DEVICES ever appeared. The walk
(`PermsModel.requestMissing`) moved on only when an answer opened the gate; Bluetooth's first answer
is TAP TO GRANT, because the central manager that raises the prompt does not know its state yet, so
the walk stopped there. The delegate said NOT ON THIS PHONE a moment later and nothing resumed the
walk. The bench pressed once and waited a fixed fifteen seconds. On a phone the same happens when
the person taps Allow: the state arrives later and nobody hears it.

No copy, light, colour, type or game timing changed. Device builds are untouched apart from item 1's
late answer, and D-292's launch gate is untouched.

1. **The walk survives a late answer** (`ui`, `Perms.kt`). The walk keeps the row it asked
   (`awaiting`, read as `walking`) until that row has a real answer, and only then goes on or stops.
   A real answer comes on the prompt's callback, which may now speak twice (the standing TAP TO GRANT,
   then the late one), or on a read of the OS (`refresh`). TAP TO GRANT is no answer and keeps the walk
   waiting. D-309's rule stands: an ASKED or REFUSED answer stops the walk, one press is one walk, and
   an answer for a row the walk is no longer waiting on moves only the row, so nothing loops. A read
   moves the walk on only when it finds the awaited row open, never stops it, because a probe still in
   flight reads ASKED. The iOS seam (`Permissions.ios.kt`) holds each Bluetooth request whose answer was
   TAP TO GRANT and answers it again when the delegate gives a real state (`bluetoothWaiting`);
   `Permissions.request`'s KDoc says `then` may be called a second time. Tests (`PermsModelTest`):
   `aLateAnswerHeardOnAReadMovesTheWalkOn` and `aLateAnswerOnThePromptsCallbackMovesTheWalkOnOnce`
   both **failed before the fix** (the walk stayed on BLUETOOTH; the second callback probed NEARBY
   DEVICES twice) and pass after; `aLateAnswerAfterTheWalkStoppedDoesNotRestartIt` holds the stop.
   Beside D-311's manager, which a refresh builds once the grant is already given, a phone that has
   granted Bluetooth answers at once; the wait is for the first ask, and the late answer goes through
   D-311's `requestStanding` like any other. ⚠️ The phone half (the person taps Allow and the walk goes
   on to NEARBY DEVICES) is unverified until a phone runs it.
2. **The simulator's NEARBY DEVICES reads NOT ON THIS PHONE** (`nearbyDevicesAskedOnThisBuild`, an
   `expect` whose simulator actual answers false and whose phone actual answers true). On the
   simulator build the row reads NOT ON THIS PHONE, as its Bluetooth row does, and nothing is probed:
   the simulator has no ranging (D-308 gives it `NoRanging`), so its probe could only ever say ASKED.
   **This is a bench accommodation**, provisional (overnight): it opens D-161's gate on simulators so
   the benches can host, the way D-292's simulator answer keeps them past the launch gate. Nothing
   about Ultra Wideband or Nearby Interaction is signed off on a simulator.
3. **The bench's setup walk waits on the rows** (`LobbyCheat.walkSetup`). It waits while the walk is
   waiting, presses REQUEST WHAT IS MISSING again when the walk stopped short or stood on one row for
   ten seconds (three presses in all), says every five seconds what it is still waiting on with each
   row's state, and gives up at a sixty-second ceiling. The bench numbers are provisional (overnight).
4. **The e2e cold-start test asserts the real refusal** (`HumanMock.swift`,
   `testTheColdStartReachesTheGateAndTheGateRefuses`). It asserted that the refusal named BLUETOOTH,
   which a simulator no longer refuses on: its BLUETOOTH reads GRANTED or NOT ON THIS PHONE, and
   NEARBY DEVICES now reads NOT ON THIS PHONE. A fresh simulator's cold start is refused on what nobody
   has answered on it, CAMERA and NOTIFICATIONS. The test resets the camera grant before launch
   (`resetAuthorizationStatus(for: .camera)`), so the cold start is cold on any simulator, and asserts
   that the refusal names CAMERA and does not name NEARBY DEVICES.
5. **The scripts** (provisional (overnight)). `e2e.sh` keeps a failed run's log and prints where;
   it used to print the path and delete the file. `e2e.sh` and `rehearse.sh` use simulators of their
   own, "E2E Seat" and "Rehearsal Seat 0" to "4", created on first use (each rehearsal seat keeps a
   different iPhone type, falling back to an iPhone 17) and shut down at the end, so neither shares
   "iPhone 17 Pro" with Gradle's iOS test runs and neither needs an "iPhone 17 Pro Max". A rehearsal
   seat that has never booted is booted once before the notification grant, as the hunt does. And the
   rehearsal's host now presses LIGHTS OUT once all five are seated (`SOMEONES_HOME_LOBBY_SEATS`): it
   pressed at three, and seats 3 and 4 were refused at the door with ROUND IN PROGRESS.
6. **The fixture meeting counts.** Every seat's ledger line on JOIN read `GATE 4/6 · READY 3/6 ·
   VOTED 4/6`, the design's `MeetingCounts()`. **No meeting screen can draw them on a housed phone**:
   `FlowModel.houseAttached` sets the counts unsaid before any push (D-247), and `HousedContentTest`
   renders every screen housed against the fixture strings. The ledger alone printed them, against
   its own rule that a count the house has not said is `-`. It now prints `-` for every count until a
   house is attached (`ScreenLedger.reading`). `ScreenLedgerTest.aCountNoHouseSentPrintsAsUnsaid`
   failed before (it read `GATE 4/6`) and passes after.
7. **The rehearsal's line probe allows the reveal** (`rehearse-check.py`, check 16, provisional
   (overnight)). With the walk fixed a rehearsal reached an ending for the first time on this Mac, and
   the check failed on seat 2, the Insider: two frames carried its own line. Both came after ROUND
   ENDED. They are the reveal, which pairs each Insider with the line they were coerced with
   (`InsiderNamed`, `gdd.md:1063`) and goes to every phone. The check now fails on any carrying frame
   before the seat's ROUND ENDED, or on a seat that was not an Insider, and names the lawful carriers.
   Verified by injection: a carrier written into seat 3's log before the ending fails it.

**The rounds.** `rehearse.sh` (seed 20260822), five seats: every seat finished setup in one press

jam reached the living, an Egress ran and resolved, and the reveal reached all five. `rehearse-check.py`:
21 of 21. Refusals in the logs, all lawful: LIGHTS OUT refused at NEEDS 3 RESIDENTS before three
were seated, and the house refused an out seat's SelectVote and LockVote (VoterOut). The bench reported
the meter bar out of reach (E-P3-4, not fixed). The radio is the house's stand-in on simulators
(D-308); nothing about contact, distance, light or a buzz is signed off here.

`tools/sim-hunt/hunt.sh` (seed 20261150), four seats: setup done in one press on all four. The round
ended for the Insiders by parity after a Revoke and a report (`SEAT 2 FOUND A REVOKED PLAYER — A
MEETING WAS CALLED`), a meeting with a vote that restrained seat 2, and no Egress, which four seats
leave no room for. The second round armed and worked (AGAIN beats). The same lawful refusals, plus
`RoundAlreadyEnded · MeetingClosed` at the ending; the Insider's own line came down only in the
reveal. `./e2e.sh` on its own seat: three cases passed and the geometry probe skipped as designed;
the old cold-start assertion, run against the new build, failed reading `THIS PHONE CANNOT TAKE A
SEAT YET / CAMERA · NOTIFICATIONS`, and its log was kept.

**Again on D-311 and D-313.** Rebased and played again: the rehearsal reached the same ending by the
same route, 21 of 21. D-311's lobby check left every bench seat in place: on a simulator BLUETOOTH
reads NOT ON THIS PHONE (D-311's manager hears `unsupported`), NEARBY DEVICES reads NOT ON THIS
PHONE, and neither is refused, so no seat's ledger ever read PERMISSIONS.

### D-315 · **The Notes app is removed: page 1 is FILES, MESSAGES, SETTINGS and CAMERA, the same for both roles — built; supersedes D-247 item 5 and D-312 item 1; nothing on the wire or in the recording changed**

**The ruling** (owner, 2026-11-21). *Let's just remove the notes app entirely.* It answers D-312 item 1,
which was provisional and for the owner to confirm: Notes had handed an Insider a line of its own one
tap from page 1, and D-312 made it the Resident's. Neither the note nor the screen it sat on is kept.
**D-247 item 5** (the housed note, *somebody was already at the marker*, provisional words) **and D-312
item 1** (Notes the same for both roles, and `NotesParityTest`) are superseded: there is no note to
word and no screen to hold parity on.

1. **The tile, the screen and the words are gone** (`ui`). The NOTES tile on page 1, `ScreenId.Notes`,
   `NotesScreen`, `PanelVals.noteLine`, the eight Resident lines, `PanelVals.HOUSED_NOTE`,
   `PanelState.noteSeed` (never set by anything; `betweenRounds` kept it as part of the evening, and
   no longer has it to keep), the tile's glyph `APP_NOTES` and `PanelIcons.Notes` (unused already).
   The Flow loses Notes' edge back to Home and its place in the springboard's set, so no walk, sweep
   or graph reaches it, and every sweep over `ScreenId.entries` (the screen renders, the layout-fault
   guard, the housed sweep) draws one screen fewer in each role.
2. **The grid closes up the way it did when TERMINAL went** (D-199: *the slot stays empty … so the
   grid keeps its shape for both roles*, built as *CAMERA moves up one slot and the row ends in two
   empty ones*). MESSAGES moves up one slot, beside FILES, and the first row ends in two empty slots;
   the second row is unchanged, SETTINGS and CAMERA and two empty slots. Two rows of four, as before.
   Tile size, spacing, ink and light are untouched. **The other arrangement**, all four tiles in one
   row with the second row gone, is a one-line change if the owner prefers it; it was not taken,
   because the grid's own precedent is that a removed tile leaves the rows as they were.
3. **Parity.** Page 1 is not allowed to differ by role (GDD M8, D-286) and does not: an Insider's and
   a Resident's render at 720×1520 are the same pixels, and the same words.
4. **Not recorded.** `ScreenId` and `PanelState` live in `ui`, which the recording never reads; the
   note was drawn on the phone and never sent or stored, and `noteSeed` was never on the wire. **The
   recording format is unchanged.** No copy, light, colour, type or timing was added or moved.

**Guards** (`PageOneTilesTest`, new): *noScreenIsNamedNotes*; *pageOneHasFourTilesAndNoNotes* (both
roles: no NOTES drawn, each of FILES, MESSAGES, SETTINGS and CAMERA drawn once, FILES and MESSAGES on
one row and SETTINGS and CAMERA on the row below in the same two columns); and
*pageOneRendersTheSameForBothRoles* (words and pixels, 720×1520 with the mockup's camera band,

trees.

**Rendered and looked at.** Page 1 at 720×1520, both roles: FILES and MESSAGES on the first row,
SETTINGS and CAMERA (inert, hatched) below, the right half of both rows empty, the widgets above and
the dock below where they were; Insider against Resident, 0 pixels differ. Against the tree before,

**Not changed, and said rather than done.** The design mockup's generator (`tools/design-mockup`,

### D-316 · **The Terminal and the couch draw the home with its counts: the plan goes to every seat at arming, and the counts ride every upload's answer, sealed, to the reader and to the couch — built (recording 48); the timelapse is STOPPED, unruled in five places; a couch on a home of two storeys or more draws the first only, awaiting a design**

**The ruling** (owner, 2026-11-21, on the overnight report's first decision): *"Yes, build it next."*
The ask: **the Terminal and the couch must show the home's map with room counts.** It answers the
overnight audit's item 1 (`rules-audit-2026-11-21.md`): the house built placements and captured each
room's count with its error (D-272) and sent none of it, so the Terminal and the couch drew D-257's
empty frame and a dash.

**Read before designing, and what each one decided here.** M11 and M12 (`gdd.md`), D-136 (inference,
knowledge first, bleed accepted), D-155 (the out are in no count, filtered by state), D-178 (the
couch's plan under a frame that keeps its height), D-186 (Static over the Terminal, ghosts exempt;
*the home plan returns to crossing to NO client*), D-199 and D-203 (the scan claims the lock; four
ways it comes free; nothing announces them), D-209 (fresh, stale and cold are Ink, Mid and Dim),
D-257, D-271 and D-272 (the plan held by the house, the captures, every tunable provisional), D-285
(nothing about counts at the couch's vote; untouched), D-145 (the couch's correlations accepted), the
occupancy spec's O3, O5, O6 and its Q1-Q5, and the owner's threat model (D-306, 2026-11-20: *what
sits only inside a player's own phone is not a leak*; what a person can see, hear or feel, and the
wire's one size and one cadence, are what is guarded).

#### Who gets what, and why

1. **The plan: every seat in the round, at arming, the same bytes** (`Effect.PlanIssued`, one per
   seat in seat order, the last run of the arming burst; `RoundMessage.PlanIssued(HomePlanView)`).
   **This amends D-186's sentence and D-271 item 2, and `epics.md:292`**: the plan now crosses, to
   everybody. Why every seat and not the reader on claiming the station, or the couch on going out:
   either of those is one frame on one phone at the moment it became the reader or left the round,
   and the frame says so on the Wi-Fi; sent to everybody at the moment everybody is sent the roster,
   it says nothing about the phone holding it. D-186's harm was a row **one class wide** (the Insider
   picker's) and the largest single disclosure in the table; this row is all four classes of a
   running round, written out, and carries rooms, names, kinds and storeys, which every player learns
   by walking the house. **It carries no card**: `HomePlanView` is still the field list (rule 3), so
   which card is in which room, the answer key to every work order (`Destination.kt`), still cannot
   cross, and nor can the stations or the T card's room. Under the owner's threat model the plan
   sitting unread in a non-reader's phone is not a leak. `HomePlanView`, `StoreyView` and `RoomView`
   become `@ClientFacing @Serializable` (D-271 said the unit answering Q1 would add the marker, the
   message and the row together; this is that unit).
2. **The Terminal's counts: the seat holding the station's lock and nobody else, while it holds it**
   (`GameState.readerHolding`, D-199, D-203). Per room in plan order, the room's latest capture this
   shift through `Observation.toView`, which cannot carry a true count: **the reported count, its
   error rolled once at capture and stored** (D-272: 15 % a missed occupant in an occupied room,
   otherwise 5 % a phantom beside an occupied room), and **the band at that beat**, from the stored
   ±5 s jitter (fresh under 15 s, stale under 45 s, cold after). A room nobody has sensed in this
   shift is **0, cold** (`gdd.md:524`: a hole and an empty room are one fact; the fixture's KDoc says
   the same). Stairs carry no count (`gdd.md:485`). **Revoked and Restrained seats are in no count**,
   because the capture counts living placed seats only (D-155); a capture taken before a Revoke still
   holds the seat, and ages out, which is `gdd.md:489`'s deniability. **The outline is the station's
   room** (`gdd.md:482`), sent as an index inside the sealed field, so no phone but the reader is
   told which room the station is in. **Released any of D-203's four ways** (the reader leaves, a
   meeting, the reader goes out, the connection drops), the next beat is nothing and the reader's
   phone drops the counts; a new claim drops any earlier visit's counts at `TerminalAnswered`, so the
   live view opens on the empty frame for up to a beat, never on old counts. **Either role, the same
   counts**: nothing in the beat reads a role, and the row is both living classes.
3. **The couch: a seat out and through a meeting since** (never a newly Revoked phone, `gdd.md:537`;
   never while a meeting runs). Per room in plan order, **the living seats the house places there at
   that beat** (`GameState.placedRoomOf`, D-136): no injected error and no band (`gdd.md:546`), so it
   is drawn in full ink. **"True" is read as the occupancy spec's Q2 reading, provisional**: the
   house's own placements, with D-136's bleed, holes and expiry, which the house cannot see past (and
   D-136 rejects a couch that reads the house perfectly); not the house's error. A Restrained seat
   is on the couch as a Revoked one is. **Static changes nothing there** (D-186).
4. **Every other phone: nothing.** Every living phone that is not the reader, every newly Revoked
   phone, every phone at a meeting.

#### How it travels: every upload's answer, one more sealed field

**No frame is added, none changes length, none changes cadence.** Every phone in a round is answered
once a beat (`RoundBody.UploadHeard`, D-263); each answer now carries **`map`**, one
`OccupancyWire` field of **196 characters**, built by `core`'s `occupancyBeat` for that seat at that
moment and **sealed under that seat's own contact seed** exactly as D-300's ranging plan is
(keystream and tag under their own domain bytes, `M` and `m`, on `RangingCodec` and its kept keys).
Without the seed the reader's counts, the couch's and nothing are the same uniform bytes, so the Wi-Fi
cannot tell who reads the Terminal or who is out, and a phone that does not open the field (another
seat's, a blank, a damaged one) draws nothing, never a partial map. A seat with no seed, or a seam
left at its default, is sent random bytes of the width, which open on no phone. **Measured over real
sockets** (`TerminalCountsWiringTest`, four phones): every upload's answer on every phone, the
reader's included, was 2 059 bytes.

**The emit schema is still the gate (rule 2).** Two kinds with rows and no effect,
`TERMINAL_READING` (both living classes, written out) and `TRUE_OCCUPANCY` (both out classes), and
`occupancyBeat` asks `EmitSchema.permits` for the seat's class before it fills the field with either:
a row deleted is an empty field on every phone. `PLAN_ISSUED` is the four classes of a running round.

**What a replay can say a phone was shown, and recording 48.** `PlanIssued` is a new effect, so the
effect rows gain one per seat at arming and a 46 build cannot name it: **recording 48**. The beats
are **not** recorded and need not be: `occupancyBeat` is a pure function of the recorded state and
the house's tick (the captures are recorded through `Sensed`, the lock through the scan and
`TerminalLeft`), so a replay computes what the reader or the couch was shown at any tick; what it
cannot say is which tick each answer was built at, which is the upload's arrival and is at most a
second apart. Events and state rows are unchanged.
**Set to 48 at integration**: built alone this was 47; D-317 took 47 for its own rows in parallel,
and the integration that put D-316, D-317 and D-318 on one tree made the combined format 48,
carrying both.

#### What the phone draws

**No new copy, light, colour or type.** The plan, the labels, the counts, the outline, the stairs
hatch and the floor strip are the fixture's, fed real data: `KitLivePlan` now draws a `LiveMap`, and
the render harness's bungalow goes through the same drawing (`LiveMap.ofFixture`) at the same
geometry. **Judgement calls where the fixture had one case and a real home has more, all provisional
and listed below**: a storey is drawn on the design's 10 by 12 cells (or its own box where larger),
centred; a count sits at the middle of its room's cells, or on the room's own cell nearest it when the
middle falls outside (an L); a label sits at the room's first cell and, for a real home, is held inside
its own run of cells and ellipsised (`EditorLabels`' rule), so a narrow room's name
never reads as the next room's; the floor strip names the plan's own storeys, one cell each, the
drawn one on the room fill. Band inks are D-209's; the couch's counts are the fixture's
`Amber.Bright`. **The couch has no outline**: a seat on the couch has no room of its own in the
house's system (D-155), and the fixture's outline there was the bungalow's.

**Allocation (rule 7), measured where it could be.** Writing an upload's answer grew from 4.4 KB to
5.6 KB (`WireDecodeAllocationTest`; its ceiling rises from 5 KB to 6 KB). The beat itself is two small
lists per answered seat and a seal in place on the desk's codec; at 18 seats that is about
18 × 1.5 KB ≈ 27 KB/s on the host, about 5 % of 0.5 MB/s, estimated by counting, not measured on a
phone. The phone opens one field a beat in place and writes its panel only when the counts change.

#### STOPPED: the timelapse, on five unruled points

The GDD's table rules the history (2:00), the speed (6×), plays once, the cooldown (2:00 from
playback end, equal to the history), the linear early-cancel cut, oldest to newest, the floor (the
round's start or the last meeting's end) and the jam's ~1.7 s of noise. **Five things it needs are
not ruled, so it is not built** and the playback stays D-257's empty frame on a housed phone:

1. **Whose cooldown**: the station's (anybody's next playback waits) or the reader's. `gdd.md:513`
   says *the only gated resource at the station*; the occupancy spec read it as the station's, unruled.
2. **What a playback frame is**: the counts as the reader would have seen them at that second, bands
   and all, or bare counts (the fixture draws every playback count in the cold ink), and how often the
   history is sampled (each second, or each capture).
3. **The TIMELAPSE control while it cools or has no history**: the live view's button reads
   *TIMELAPSE . 2:00 AT 6X* and has no designed state, words or light for a cooldown, for a history
   of a few seconds after a meeting, or for a refusal.
4. **F-008's numeral count-up** (`gdd.md:996`) against rule 5 and D-202's *no local animation*
   (the occupancy spec's Q4).
5. **What ends a playback early**: D-203 frees the station at a meeting, so a meeting stops a
   playback; whether that counts as an early cancel (and cuts the cooldown) is not said.

**Also STOPPED, smaller: a couch on a home of two storeys or more.** `gdd.md:546` says *every
storey*; the fixture draws one storey under a strip that takes no taps, and nothing designs two on
the couch. The couch draws the **first storey**, the strip naming them all; every storey's counts are
already in the field, so only the drawing waits. **And the Terminal draws the station's storey**,
which the fixture's layout says (the floor you are on, filled) and the GDD does not (the occupancy
spec's Q3): counts upstairs are not visible from a station downstairs.

#### Judgement calls, all provisional, owner to confirm

- The plan to **every** seat at arming (above), amending D-186, D-271 item 2 and `epics.md:292`.
- "True occupancy" is the house's placements without the error (the spec's Q2 reading).
- A hole is 0 in the cold ink.
- The couch draws no outline.
- The live view shows the empty frame for up to one beat after the scan, before the first counts.
- Real homes' labels are held inside their room and ellipsised (the editor's rule); counts sit in
  their own room's cells; storeys draw at the design's cell size, centred.
- `OccupancyWire.MAX_ROOMS` is 128: a home with more rooms draws its later rooms empty (a home
  painted in the editor's 10 by 12 grid has at most 120 squares a storey).
- The reader is still not a sensor while reading (D-272 item 6, unchanged): only its 3 s sweep on the
  T scan captures the station's room.

#### Guards, each proven by breaking it

- `OccupancyBeatTest` (core, the real pipeline): only the reader is sent counts; the counts are the
  stored capture's reported count and its band through fresh, stale and cold, asked twice the same; a
  hole is 0 cold and the outline is the station's room; over 200 captures the reader's counts carry
  the injected error; a Revoked seat is in no capture, the couch is shown the house's placements live
  and loses an expired sighting, a newly Revoked phone and a meeting are shown nothing, a Restrained
  seat is on the couch; leaving the station, a meeting or a Revoke stops the counts; a Static changes
  neither the reader's beat nor the couch's; an Insider reader and a Resident reader get the same beat
  and the same sealed bytes, and every kind is one width.
  **Injected: the counts sent to every living seat** (`reads = running && !state.isOut(seat) && …`):
  *seat 0, not the reader, was sent Terminal(here=0, counts=[0, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], bands=[2, 0, 2, 2,
  2, 2, 2]) expected:<Nothing> but was:<Terminal(…)>* and *the reader left and was still sent counts*.
  **Injected: the `TERMINAL_READING` row deleted from the schema**: five of the seven fail, the first
  *the reader was sent no counts. Expected value to be of type <…OccupancyBeat$Terminal>, actual
  <…OccupancyBeat$Nothing>*: the schema fails closed.
- `OccupancyWireTest` (model): every kind seals to one width and opens to itself; another seat's seed,
  a blank and one flipped character open to nothing; a band past cold, an unknown kind, a byte past
  the rooms, an outline on the couch's and anything in a nothing all read as nothing.
- `TerminalCountsWiringTest` (app, four phones over real sockets, `SimulatedAir`): the plan reaches
  every phone, the same plan, the house's; BRUNO performs with DEVI a metre away, CYRUS scans T and
  holds the station, and CYRUS's panel holds the house's counts (STUDY: capture true 2, reported 2,
  sent 2; HALL 1 from the T scan's sweep; the outline HALL); no other phone holds the Terminal's or
  the couch's counts; every upload's answer on every phone is 2 059 bytes; leaving the station clears
  CYRUS's counts. **Injected
  over the sockets, the counts sent to every living seat**: *ALBA, not the reader, holds the
  Terminal's counts. Expected value to be null, but was: <Terminal(here=2, counts=[0, 0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 0,
  0, 0, 0, 0], bands=[2, 2, 0, 2, 0, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2])>.* The answer lengths stayed equal under the
  injection, which is the seal doing its job: on the Wi-Fi a leaked reading and nothing look alike, so
  the panel is what the guard reads.
- `EmitSchemaTest`: `PLAN_ISSUED` is the one plan kind and the four classes of a running round;
  `TERMINAL_READING` both living, `TRUE_OCCUPANCY` both out. It replaces *no kind in the table
  carries the home's plan*, which D-186 wrote and this entry overrules.
- `StaticTest`: the arming burst is nine runs, the plan last, one per seat and one plan.
- `HomePlanViewFieldsTest`: the serializer's fields are exactly the view's (`storeys, rooms`;
  `name, cols, rows, cells`; `name, kind`); it replaces *the plan view has no serializer*.
- `HousedMapRenderTest` (ui): through `houseSaid(PlanIssued)` and `occupancySaid`, the housed Terminal
  draws the bench home with the bench reader's counts and inks; a jam veils it with the plan still
  under; the couch draws true occupancy clean under a jam with no outline; a one-storey home with an
  L-shaped room draws its own names, its count inside the L, and none of the bungalow's.

- **Guards this entry overrules, rewritten rather than deleted.** `OccupancyRecordingTest` held that
  *no client is sent one byte more for the plan or the map*; it now holds that every seat's
  transcript is the same with and without the plan and the map's input **but for one `PlanIssued` row
  per seat, the same plan on every seat**, and that the map's input still makes no effect.
  `FuzzPropertyTest` names `TrueOccupancy` among the out-only kinds; `HouseBuzzTest` and
  `RoundWireTest` build a `PlanIssued` and leave the two beat kinds out of their effect sweeps; the
  recording tests pin `recording/48`; `WireDecodeAllocationTest`'s answer ceiling is 6 KB.

**Rendered and looked at** (`ui/build/screens/d316-*.png`, 600 by 1300). **The live view**
(`d316-terminal-live`): the bench home's GROUND storey with its own gaps between rooms, GROUND filled
on the strip and UPPER beside it; HALL outlined in two-unit ink on the room fill with its name in ink
and **1**; STUDY **2** in ink; KITCHEN, LIVING and GARAGE **0** in the dim ink; STAIRS hatched with
no number; the motion budget and the TIMELAPSE button below, as before. **Jammed**
(`d316-terminal-jammed`): the noise field over the plan, fragments of the labels and the stairs hatch
showing through, the strip and the foot clean. **The couch** (`d316-couch`, handed a jam it may not
receive): the two meters (SYSTEM INTEGRITY with no number pushed, the Egress box empty), the strip,
the same plan with HALL **1**, STUDY **2** and the rest **0**, every count in full ink, no outline,
no noise. **A home that is not the bungalow** (`d316-terminal-other-home`): ONLY FLOOR on a one-cell
strip, a 6 by 5 storey at the design's cell size centred in the frame, the L-shaped PANTRY with its
name cut to *P…* inside its one-cell column and its **3** in the stale ink inside the L's foot,
HALLWAY outlined with **1**, STAIRS hatched. **Every one of the 219 fixture renders of the screenshot
sweep (`termlive`, `timelapse` and `ghost3` in both roles among them) is byte-identical to the tree
before this change**, so the bungalow goes through the new drawing unchanged.

| site | what it said | what it says now |
|---|---|---|

| `model` `Effect.PlanIssued`, `RoundMessage.PlanIssued`, `EmitSchema.PLAN_ISSUED` | (none) | one per seat at arming; row: the four classes of a running round |
| `model` `EmitSchema.TERMINAL_READING`, `TRUE_OCCUPANCY`, `BEAT_KINDS` | (none) | the beat's two kinds: both living; both out |

### D-317 · **DISCUSSION, EGRESS TIMER and REVOKE COOLDOWN are the host's lobby settings, locked at arming and stamped into the recording; each offers its current number alone until the owner rules a range — built (recording 48)**

**The ruling** (owner, 2026-11-21). *"We should build this"*, of the three lobby rows that were fixed
text while INSIDERS and VOTING took a press: **DISCUSSION 90S**, **EGRESS TIMER 120S** (a literal on
the row, `Balance.EGRESS_TIMER` behind it) and **REVOKE COOLDOWN 60S**. D-037 already said what
happens to them once they are settings: *balance values lock at arming and are stamped into the
recording*, *or whoever runs the server can shorten their own Revoke cooldown mid-round*.

**The values, and where they come from.**

| row | default and only choice | ruled by | range / step |
|---|---|---|---|
| DISCUSSION | **90 s** | `gdd.md:431` (*90s (lobby setting)*), `:930`, `:1186` | **unruled** |
| EGRESS TIMER | **120 s** | D-014; F-009; `gdd.md:370`, `:382`, `:1184`, A-1 | **unruled** |
| REVOKE COOLDOWN | **60 s** | the lobby row; `Balance.REVOKE_COOLDOWN`, confirmed 60 s by E-L5-1 (20 Hz); `gdd.md:930` lists it among the host's options | **unruled** |

`gdd.md:1181`'s *Initial 45s* is the opening Revoke cooldown F-004 proposed, which D-132 replaced with
*half the normal duration*; it is not this row's number and was not used.

**Built as VOTING is built, row for row** (D-117's road):

1. **The control** (`ui`). Each row draws through the same `LobbyRow`, with the same tap and the same
   look as VOTING: a press on the host's phone, nothing on a guest's. `LobbyModel` holds each number
   (`discussionSeconds`, `egressTimerSeconds`, `revokeCooldownSeconds`), cycles it through its list
   (`DISCUSSIONS`, `EGRESS_TIMERS`, `REVOKE_COOLDOWNS`) and hands it to `LobbyLink.setDiscussion`,
   `setEgressTimer` and `setRevokeCooldown`. **Each list holds the row's current number and nothing
   else**, because no ruling gives a range or a step: the press reaches the desk, the number does not
   move, and a range the owner rules is a list that grows and nothing else.
2. **The desk and the arming** (`platform`, `app`). `LobbyDesk` holds the three beside
   `voteWindowSeconds`; `LobbyHouse.armingInputs` reads them in the same instant as everything else;
   `RoundAuthority` hands them to `armingFor`; `Event.RoundArmed` carries `discussionSeconds`,
   `egressTimerSeconds` and `revokeCooldownSeconds`; `GameState` holds them for the round. **No lobby
   message**: like VOTING, nothing goes down the lobby wire, and the clients learn each number on the
   push that starts its clock.
3. **The rules read the locked value, never `Balance`** (`core`, `app`). An Egress starts at
   `state.egressTimer`; an arm spends `state.revokeCooldown`; every seat's Revoke opens at half of it at
   LIGHTS OUT and at every meeting's end (`Balance.opening`, the one `/ 2`); the house's clock closes
   the talk on `state.discussionSeconds`. `Balance.DISCUSSION_SECONDS`, `EGRESS_TIMER(_SECONDS)` and
   `REVOKE_COOLDOWN(_SECONDS)` are now only the defaults a round armed without a setting gets.
4. **The phones draw the locked value** (the wire). Three existing effects widen, the same number to
   every seat, so there is nothing role-shaped in any of them: `MeetingPhaseOpened` gains
   `discussionSeconds` (the talk's push only, null elsewhere, `voteWindowSeconds`' shape);
   `OpeningMessage` and `MeetingEnded` gain `revokeCooldown`, in ticks, which page 2's Revoke bar is half
   of and an Insider's own arm holds for in full (D-239, D-286). The Egress already arrives as the
   `remaining` it opened with; the one place a phone fell back to the default timer (an `EgressHeld`
   for a phone that missed the fire) now draws against the house's number instead. **No new `Effect`**:
   the schema is per kind, the three kinds keep their audiences (every seat), so nothing fails closed
   and nothing new opens.
5. **The recording** (`harness`). **Format 46 → 48**: the arming row and every state row gain
   `discussion=`, `egressTimer=` and `revokeCooldown=` (seconds), and the parser defaults none of them,
   so a version 46 arming row is refused; the `MeetingPhaseOpened` effect row gains `discussion=`, and
   `OpeningMessage` and `MeetingEnded` gain `revokeCooldown=`.
   **Set to 48 at integration**: built alone this was 47; D-316 took 47 for its `PlanIssued` rows in
   parallel, and the integration that put D-316, D-317 and D-318 on one tree made the combined format
   48, carrying both.

**No copy, light, colour or type was added.** The three rows keep their labels and their values; what
changed is that a press on the host's phone reaches the house.

**Not built, and why.** *The app should propose the default from the map* (D-014, `gdd.md:384`): no
ruling says how the longest marker-to-marker path becomes seconds (D-014 gives the idea and *a house
twice the size gets twice the suggested timer*, with no base and no rate), so there is no proposal.

**For the owner to rule** (each row offers its current number alone until then):

- **DISCUSSION**: the range and the step.
- **EGRESS TIMER**: the range and the step; and whether the map proposes the default, and if so the
  seconds per cell (or per hop) of the longest marker-to-marker path.
- **REVOKE COOLDOWN**: the range and the step.
- **Two bounds a range would have to respect**, written in the code and checked nowhere for a host
  setting: the Egress cooldown (180 s) must outlive the Egress timer (`egressFired`'s note), and the
  Revoke cooldown must outlive the 20 s arm window (`Balance.REVOKE_ARM_WINDOW`).
- **Already true of VOTING, and now of these three**: a guest's lobby row draws its own phone's number,
  not the host's, because the setting never goes down the lobby wire. With one choice per row the two
  agree; with a range they would not, until the round starts and the house's pushes take over.

**Guards** (new): `LobbySettingsTest` (`core`): the arming locks all three; a 60 s EGRESS TIMER gives
an Egress a 60 s deadline and 60 s `remaining` on every phone; a 60 s DISCUSSION is published on the
talk's push and on no other; a 30 s REVOKE COOLDOWN opens every seat at 15 s, an arm spends 30 s, a
meeting's end reopens at 15 s, and LIGHTS OUT and the meeting's end carry it. `LobbySettingsArmingTest`
(`app`): the desk hands the three to the arming; each locks at arming and the desk moving mid-round
moves nothing; the house closes a 60 s talk at 60 s. `LobbySettingsTest` (`ui`): each row offers the
ruled number alone; the host's press reaches the house and a guest's reaches nothing; a phone draws
the Revoke clock, its own arm and the talk's clock from the pushed numbers. `LobbySettingsRecordingTest`
(`harness`): each is stamped on the arming row and every state row, survives the text form and
replays; an arming row missing any one is fatal; every seat is sent the same cooldown.

**Proved by injection.** The rules and the house's clock were made to read `Balance`'s defaults instead
of the locked values (`Balance.EGRESS_TIMER`, `Balance.REVOKE_COOLDOWN`, `Balance.REVOKE_OPENING`,
`Balance.DISCUSSION_SECONDS`); quoted from the XML:
*the house armed a 60 s talk and opened a 90 s one expected:<60> but was:<90>*;
*seat 0's Revoke reopened at the default's half, not the locked cooldown's expected:<Tick(step=500)> but was:<Tick(step=800)>*;
*the house armed a 60 s Egress timer and ran an Egress to Tick(step=4200) expected:<Tick(step=3000)> but was:<Tick(step=4200)>*;
*seat 0's Revoke opened at Tick(step=600), not at half of the 30 s the round was armed with expected:<Tick(step=300)> but was:<Tick(step=600)>*;
*a 60 s talk did not close at sixty seconds, so the house ran its own ninety. Expected <1>, actual <0>.*
Restored, all green. One test written for the Egress's expiry stayed green under the injection (the
rules take `EgressExpired` whenever it arrives, so it measured nothing) and was deleted.

**Rendered and looked at** (720×1520). The host's lobby: INSIDERS UNKNOWN, INSIDERS KNOW EACH OTHER ON,
SUBROUTINES EACH 7, DISCUSSION 90S, VOTING 45S, EGRESS TIMER 120S, REVOKE COOLDOWN 60S, in the rows'
existing type and rules, unchanged after a press on each of the three; then YOUR ONE LINE, LIGHTS OUT
and CLOSE THE HOUSE. The guest's: the same seven rows and values, LEAVE THIS HOUSE, no LIGHTS OUT.

**Checked** (on the final tree, `*/build/test-results` cleared first: `./gradlew check --continue`
with the two variant sweeps excluded, then `:app:variantSweepRelease`, then `:app:variantSweepPlaytest`,
the app's XML copied out after each, every result XML counted with a python glob): model 356 (JVM) +
340 (iOS Simulator); core 425 + 423; platform 211; harness 136; ui 778 (desktop) + 386 (iOS
Simulator); app 280 (the default variant), 173 (Release), 280 (Playtest). 0 failures, 0 errors, 0
skipped; 3,335 in the default check. The four new suites are in the XML, `LobbySettingsArmingTest` in
all three app variants.

### D-318 · **A card read goes up as its id and the house routes it: paper this home never registered is NOT A MARKER, on that phone only, outside the recording — built; answers D-313's stop; the uplink and the downlink changed, the recording did not (46)**

**The ruling** (owner, 2026-11-21). *Make sense* — to D-313's proposal: one raw read from the scan,
routed by `routeScan` at the authority, and a scanner-only unregistered answer that is not recorded.
The proposal recommended D-160's *no* for NOT A MARKER and the owner agreed to it; it is built
**provisional**. D-313 found the contradiction: a card this home never registered went up as
`BeginSubroutine`, so the rules placed its reader at a card that is no place in the home, spent
their open Subroutine and answered NOTHING FOR YOU HERE where D-124 reserves NOT A MARKER; a mislaid
or spare meeting card called a meeting, because `CallMeeting` carried no card and nothing checked
it; and `routeScan` was called by nothing but its own test, because a phone has no map.

1. **One raw read.** Every decoded in-round scan goes up as `Asked.Read(card)`, the card's id and
   nothing else, in the upload's request slot: one shape and, in the fixed-width slot, one size on
   every phone and for both roles. `inRoundScan` decodes and returns the id, with no shape test, the
   meeting card's included. The house routes it: `IntentDesk.Landing.Read` → `LobbyHouse.onCardRead`
   → `HouseDoors.read` → `RoundAuthority.cardRead`, which calls `routeScan` against the home the
   round was armed in. A registered card, the Terminal and every Egress node go to the rules as the
   `MarkerScanned` they always were (placement, D-124's resolution, D-199, D-297); the registered
   meeting card is the `MeetingCalled` it always was (D-121, refused by the gate as before during an
   Egress or from an out seat). **`routeScan` now takes the card's id and never its shape**: the shape
   is printed on the same paper and is not what makes a card part of a home.
   **`IntentMessage.BeginSubroutine` and `IntentMessage.CallMeeting` are deleted from the wire**, and
   `Intent.BeginSubroutine`, `Intent.CallMeeting` and their `factOf` arms with them. Kept, either
   would be one forged frame away from the bug this closes, and `IntentMessage`'s own rule — *an
   Intent may exist only where the event it becomes needs nothing but the phone* — already said a
   card read fails it: which fact a card is needs the map. A card read is `RoundBody.Fire`'s case
   with the map as the second source, so it has a member of its own beside `Asked.Fire`.
   `IntentAdmissionTest` moves `MarkerScanned` and the card's `MeetingCalled` from *requestable* to
   *house-composed*. A read outside a round does not go up (no seed, no map; the phone's log says so).
2. **Unregistered → NOT A MARKER, to that phone only.** A new effect, `Effect.CardUnregistered(seat)`,
   projected as `RoundMessage.CardUnregistered`, which carries nothing: the socket is the address.
   **Schema row `CARD_UNREGISTERED` to the two living classes, addressed to the scanning seat** —
   `SCAN_ANSWERED`'s row and for its reason: narrowed to either role it would be a role test anyone
   could run with a scrap of paper, and the out classes get nothing because their registered scans
   get nothing on this axis either. The phone moves to the screen it already had,
   `ScreenId.ScanUnknown`, and changes nothing else (`FlowModel.housePushed`): its caught work and its
   tap control stand, because nothing at the house moved. **The seat is not placed, its open
   Subroutine is not spent, no meeting is called, and no other phone is sent anything.** The answer
   is built from the card and the map and never from a role, so the same paper is the same bytes on
   an Insider's phone and a Resident's.
3. **Not recorded, and that is D-072 rather than a gap.** The recording is what reached the rules:
   events, the effects the rules produced from them, the states, and the gate's refusals. Unregistered
   paper never reaches the rules, so it makes no event and no row. `CardUnregistered` is the one
   effect the rules never produce: the house builds it above them and hands it to the emit boundary
   directly, so the schema still decides who may receive it, and `RoundAuthority` keeps it in
   `answeredOutsideTheRules`, apart from `emitted`. A count of unregistered cards, in a recording or
   anywhere else, is the arbiter of a player's claim D-072 refuses: *everything a player saw is theirs
   to report, or to lie about.*
4. **The buzz.** NOT A MARKER carries D-160's *no*, two vibrates (`Haptic.Double`), on that phone
   only, the kind's own value read by `HouseBuzzer` off the effect and the message alike; **provisional**.
   The acquire keeps its *yes*, one Short, which is the scan window's and is unchanged (D-159, D-160).
   NOTHING FOR YOU HERE stays silent; whether it should say *no* too is the open line on the phone
   checklist, as before.
5. **A meeting card from the house's own deck that this home did not register** is unregistered, so
   NOT A MARKER and no meeting (D-169). So is a mislaid card. Only the id on the map calls a meeting.
6. **The recording format is unchanged, at 46.** No event, effect row or state row changed shape,
   and `reduce` reduces every event exactly as before: `MarkerScanned` and `MeetingCalled` are the same
   events, and the routing above the rules only decides which reads become them. `Transcript` renders
   `CardUnregistered` (the per-client transcripts read every effect a phone is sent), but no
   recording can hold that row, because the rules never emit it. A version 46 recording made before
   this change, unregistered `MarkerScanned` and all, replays exactly as it did.
   **In the combined tree the format is 48** (D-316 and D-317, integrated with this entry); D-318
   moved nothing in it either way (D-320).
7. **No new copy, light, colour or type.** NOT A MARKER and its screen already existed (D-124);
   nothing on it was touched.

**Guards.** `CardReadTest` (app, new), in process on the real `RoundAuthority` in the bench's home:
*anUnregisteredCardIsNotAMarkerOnThatPhoneOnlyAndNothingElseHappens* (one `CardUnregistered` to that
seat through the real schema, the state the same object so no event reached the rules, the rules'
effects and refusals unchanged, the open work and the placement unchanged, no meeting);
*aSpareMeetingCardCallsNoMeetingAndIsNotAMarker*; *aRegisteredCardOfEveryKindRoutesAsBefore* (work
opens and places, the Terminal is the station, an Egress node answers nothing and places, the
registered meeting card calls the meeting, none of them NOT A MARKER); *anInsiderAndAResidentAreAnsweredAlike*
(the same message, the same class, the same buzz); *theAcquireSaysYesAndNotAMarkerSaysNo* (one motor:
the window's Short, then the house's Double); and, **over real loopback sockets**, a five-phone evening,
*overTheWireNotAMarkerIsThatPhonesAloneAndTheMeetingCardStillCalls*: a Resident and then an Insider
catch their own work, read a stray card and a spare meeting card, and each lands on NOT A MARKER
with one *no*, the other four phones sent nothing in two beats, the rules emitted nothing for that
seat, its work and placement unchanged, no meeting, the two roles' wires the same; then the
registered meeting card rings every phone. `ScanRoutingTest`: *a spare meeting card from the deck
calls no meeting*. `EmitSchemaTest`: *not a marker reaches the scanning seat of either living role
and nobody else*. `IntentWireTest`: *aCardCannotBeNamedAsWorkOrAsTheMeetingFromAPhone* (the two old
frames no longer decode; the read carries a card and no shape). `NotAMarkerRender` (ui, new).

**Proved red by injection.** The unregistered branch of `RoundAuthority.cardRead` made to put the
card to the rules as work again (`gate(Event.MarkerScanned(…))`), then restored: four of
`CardReadTest`'s six went red, quoted from the XML: *an unregistered card was not answered NOT A
MARKER, once, to that seat (D-124, D-318). Expected <[CardUnregistered(seat=Seat(index=2))]>, actual
<[ScanAnswered(seat=Seat(index=2), opened=null), PresenceChanged(seat=Seat(index=2),
at=MarkerId(value=ZZZZ001), open=false)]>*; *a spare meeting card reached the rules*; the role
comparison (*Expected <[CardUnregistered]>, actual <[ScanAnswered(opened=null)]>*); and over the
wire *never happened: Resident was told NOT A MARKER … SCAN OPENED NOTHING*, which is D-313's defect
exactly.

**Rendered and looked at.** NOT A MARKER in a round, 600×1300 with an iPhone 16 Pro's insets,
through `FlowHost`, after a Jam was caught and left by NOT THIS ONE: the shared refusal frame, the
struck circle, NOT A MARKER, SCAN ANOTHER and SEE MY SUBROUTINES, the status bar ARMED with the
meter's honest dash. An Insider's and a Resident's are the same pixels, and the caught work is still
held (`build/screens/notamarker-in-round-*.png`).

| site | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `model` `IntentWire.kt`, `Intent.kt` | `BeginSubroutine`, `CallMeeting` | deleted |
| `model` `RequestSlot.kt` | `Asked.Act`, `Asked.Fire` | + `Asked.Read(card)` |
| `model` `Effect.kt`, `RoundWire.kt`, `EmitSchema.kt` | (none) | `CardUnregistered`, its message, its row (living, the seat) |
| `core` `Scanning.kt` | `routeScan(…, card: MarkerCard, …)`, called by a test | takes the id; called by the house |
| `core` `Intents.kt` | `factOf` arms for the two | deleted |
| `platform` `IntentDesk.kt` | `Put`, `Draw`, `Duplicate` | + `Landing.Read` |
| `app` `RoundAuthority.kt`, `HouseDoors.kt`, `LobbyOverTransport.kt` | (none) | `cardRead`, `read`, `onCardRead` |
| `app` `RoundOverTransport.kt`, `RoundClient.kt`, `Cheats.kt`, `RoundCheat.kt` | the read split by shape on the phone | `readCard(id)` |
| `app` `HouseBuzzer.kt` | (none) | `CardUnregistered` buzzes `Double` |
| `ui` `Flow.kt` | (none) | `CardUnregistered` → `ScanUnknown` |
| `harness` `Transcript.kt` | (none) | renders the effect; no recording holds it |
